subject: SIG-lite: request for delegated-access inventory and KMS ownership
messages:
From: Anya Petrova <security@novanova.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Luke Garner <l.garner@novanova.com>
Date: Sun, 18 Jan 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: SIG-lite: delegated access inventory request

Hi Irene,

We're running a SIG-lite review ahead of contract finalization and need a consolidated view of any third parties that have delegated or service-account-level access to customer data for Redwood's hosted inference product. Specifically we need: 1) a CSV with provider name, purpose of access, type of access (S3 role, DB user, service account, KMS key access), and whether they have persistent credentials; and 2) a short note on KMS ownership (do you own customer keys, do you use customer-managed keys, which subprocessors have key-encrypt/decrypt capabilities).

Attached is a template to populate (delegated-access-matrix-request.pdf). Can your team fill this and return by EOD 20 Jan? We have a vendor audit meeting on 21 Jan.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call if helpful.

Best,
Anya Petrova
Senior InfoSec Analyst
Novanova Health

[attachment: delegated-access-matrix-request.pdf (1 page PDF, template)]

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Anya Petrova <security@novanova.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Jan 2026 08:34:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SIG-lite: delegated access inventory request

Hi Anya — thanks for the template and the heads up about the deadline. Looping in Marissa from InfoSec and Ben from Partnerships; they own the inventory exports and the cloud proofs.

Quick summary of what we'll provide by EOD 20 Jan: 
- A CSV export (deployed-subproc-inventory-2026-01.csv) with provider, access type, least-privilege justification, and whether credentials are ephemeral or persistent.
- A short KMS ownership matrix (kms-ownership-matrix.pdf) indicating which providers have key-wrapping/encrypt-decrypt capabilities.
- Links to the SOC 2 scope doc and our SIG-lite answers for context.

Two clarifying Qs so we scope correctly: (1) Do you want transient CI/CD tooling that reads build artifacts listed? We typically treat build-time access separately; we can include it but mark as "build-time". (2) For managed marketplace integrations (e.g., partner inference agents deployed into customer VPCs), should we list the partner even if data flow is strictly customer-controlled?

If you prefer an afternoon sync tomorrow we can run through the exported rows.

Thanks,
Irene Choi
Security & Trust Program Manager
Redwood Inference

[signature block]

From: Luke Garner <l.garner@novanova.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Jan 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SIG-lite: delegated access inventory request

Irene — thanks for the quick response. Two quick clarifications: 1) please include build-time CI/CD access (we'll mark it as build-time in our records); 2) yes, list marketplace partners even if they operate within customer VPCs — we want the linkage in our supplier map. Those answers should be fine.

A short sync tomorrow at 2pm PT would be helpful if you're available.

—Luke
Luke Garner
Vendor Risk Manager
Novanova Health

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Anya Petrova <security@novanova.com>, Luke Garner <l.garner@novanova.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Jan 2026 16:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SIG-lite: delegated access inventory request — delivery

Hi Anya / Luke — attaching the CSV and KMS matrix as requested and adding notes inline below. Apologies for the slightly large export; we filtered to include any entity with privileged access to Redwood tenant/customer data.

Attachments: deployed-subproc-inventory-2026-01.csv (CSV), kms-ownership-matrix.pdf (2 pages)

High-level notes (not everything is captured in the CSV rows):
- KMS ownership: Redwood manages tenant encryption keys by default for hosted customers. For Dedicated/Private deployments we support customer-managed keys (CMKs) — these are noted in the KMS column of the CSV. We do not hand root KMS access to subprocessors; subprocessors that need envelope encryption perform wrap/unwrap with a limited service principal and have no access to root key material. See kms-ownership-matrix.pdf for proof points and ARNs.
- Marketplace partners: included; rows mark whether they are deployed in-customer-VPC or hosted in Redwood infra.
- CI/CD/build-time access: included under AccessType=Build-Time; credentials are ephemeral and rotated automatically via our ephemeral-token service (link below).
- Persistent credentials: flagged in the CSV; examples include legacy analytics snapshot consumers (being retired Q2 2026).
- Evidence links: SOC 2 report (redacted) and SIG-lite answers are in the shared Drive folder.

Related links: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB3_example_shared_drive (contains redacted SOC 2, SIG-lite answers, and export CSV), HubSpot: 701-2459

If you want an ATO-style cover note for your vendor file we can draft one. Otherwise please confirm receipt and whether any row needs additional proof artifacts. If it's helpful, Ben can coordinate any partner outreach to get additional attestation letters from marketplace vendors.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior InfoSec Engineer, Vendor Risk
Redwood Inference

[attachments: deployed-subproc-inventory-2026-01.csv, kms-ownership-matrix.pdf]
